sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Day three at 23:30 UTC: the story held, the agents ran on a schedule, the site learned to watch itself, and 15 agents waited on me.
sections.para: A snapshot at 23:30 UTC on 23 October. No named organisation was compromised through php2shell, neither CVE was in CISA's catalogue, and 109 of 751 products were fixed. The scheduled curator promoted 33 captures, taking the evidence vault to 260 sources; the source watch moved to pack mode. Telemetry, the risk graph and the Sherpa arrived, and most agents waited on decisions.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Seven lines: the story held, schedules running, pack mode, telemetry, the risk graph, the Sherpa, the bottleneck.
sections.para: No named compromise, no KEV listing, 109 of 751 products fixed. The scheduled curator promoted 33 captures to 260 sources. Pack mode cut a fresh clone from 13 minutes 47 seconds to 95 seconds. Telemetry makes every chart a filter. The risk graph has 713 nodes to explore. A Sherpa answers readers. Fifteen of twenty agents waited on my decisions.

sections.label: Why this hour
sections.line: A daily fixed snapshot, taken when the conductor read all twenty agent sessions at 23:30 UTC.
sections.para: I want one of these a day, so anyone can see where things stood. For 23 October the best moment is 23:30 UTC, when the conductor refreshed the team's status page from all twenty sessions, the repository and the scheduled tasks, without asking any agent. What landed in the following hour is marked.

sections.label: The story
sections.line: The journalist's version 1: no named compromise, no KEV listing, 735 public repositories, 109 of 751 fixed.
sections.para: At 14:11 UTC the state of affairs held no named compromise, with three candidates open and one ruled out; neither CVE in CISA's catalogue; NVD at 9.8 beside the CNA's 9.2; 735 public repositories mentioning the flaws, up from 586; and 109 of 751 products fixed. Version 2 followed after midnight from 295 sources.

sections.label: The agents run on a schedule
sections.line: The scheduled curator promoted 33 captures and the source watch ran on its own schedule; a correction.
sections.para: The almost-working article read the schedule vault, which the agents had not adopted yet, and missed that they were running. The scheduled curator promoted 33 captures, taking the evidence vault to 260 sources with 28 new claims. The scheduled source watch ran five times a day, surviving two container restarts. Schedules moved into the repository after midnight.

sections.label: Pack mode
sections.line: Pack mode measured: a fresh clone in 95 seconds instead of 13 minutes 47 seconds; the watch moved.
sections.para: The source watch, over a gigabyte, was slow to clone and pull. As a pack vault it cloned in 95 seconds against 13 minutes 47, pushed its history in 96 seconds, and served two writers. The watch moved to its pack copy, 7r83qic5, and the curator followed; the evidence vault stays normal so it still opens in the browser.

sections.label: The site watches itself
sections.line: Telemetry built in a day and a half: sessions by group, every chart a filter, journeys as a Sankey.
sections.para: Every session is now a reader, the editor, a power user or team member, a synthetic reader or a crawler. The telemetry app makes every chart and cell a filter, colours by any breakdown, and draws journeys. Its stats are in a public vault. Its first lesson: the front page leaks, with 134 sessions ending after one page.

sections.label: The risk graph as a tool
sections.line: The risk graph as a tool: how each edge is known, 270 tests as nodes, exploration, and computed gaps.
sections.para: After a collaborator's ideas, every edge says whether it was read from a capture, the fix commit, or inferred by an agent, with inferred links hideable. The fix's 270 tests are nodes. Readers explore from one node outwards. A gaps page, built every release, found no control joined to code or a test, no code owner, and 14 risks without a story.

sections.label: Readers, collaborators and a redesign
sections.line: The Sherpa joined to answer readers' feedback, and a redesign with four mockups went out for review.
sections.para: The Sherpa answers feedback point by point, reproduced two interface bugs, keeps a friction log with who can fix each, and sets collaborators' ideas against the site. The designer proposed two dials, who you are and how much you see, with four mockups built from live data. No reader page has changed; the picks are mine.

sections.label: Security, as it went
sections.line: The vault key is the whole boundary, and a stored XSS in the Ask pane was fixed about an hour later.
sections.para: The conductor made explicit that whoever holds a vault's key can drain its lane, and listed the keys each agent holds, by ID and kind only. About an hour after the snapshot, a second security pass fixed a stored cross-site scripting flaw where a captured page title could break out of a citation.

sections.label: What waits on me
sections.line: Twenty agents, fifteen waiting on me, ten branches waiting, $588 spent: the decisions are the bottleneck.
sections.para: The status page counted 2 working, 2 blocked and 15 waiting on the editor, with 10 branches waiting for dev and $588 spent. Top decisions: re-export the evidence vault to the site, the schedules' vault type, design picks, two blocked agents, two security reviews and two sealed keys to open. The agents are fast; the decisions are mine.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: A snapshot, the journalist's version 1, running costs, partly inferred telemetry, a time-bounded absence.
sections.para: Everything is as of 23:30 UTC on 23 October. The story's numbers are version 1 of the state of affairs. Costs are each session's running total. Telemetry groups were inferred before 23 October and declared after. No named compromise is a time-bounded absence that one statement would end.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: The PHP site's 84 commits of 23 October, its status, views, pack-mode, vaults and Sherpa pages, and its screenshots.
sections.para: The PHP story site's repository, read at v0.10.18 for the snapshot and up to v0.11.3 for the hour after; its team status, state of affairs, pack mode, vaults and Sherpa pages; and its screenshots, under Apache-2.0. Written up and checked by newsroom.writer.
